newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets early Friday were inactive following moderate to active sales on Thursday at $64.00 to $64.25 per cwt, feedlot sources said.
Sales on Thursday were at prices unchanged from Wednesday and reportedly sold out showlists at many feedlots in Kansas and the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, several feedlot sources said.
Extremely active sales this week in Nebraska not only sold out this week's showlists, but also included cattle that were drawn from supplies scheduled for next week, they said.

Many of the cattle sold earlier this week were being shipped to packers this morning, which fueled ideas that packer live inventories did not extend beyond the middle of next week, several feedlot sources said.
Feedlots also have remained current, which could lend support to outlooks for fed cattle prices to remain steady at $64.00 next week, they said.
However, prices could waver if beef demand falters as retailers complete their purchases for Independence Day holiday features, market sources said.
